title: Contractive scalar units in continuous integral coefficients
statement: Let ℓ be prime and E a normed field with a normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra structure. For any scheme X, a commutative internal ring R isomorphic by a ring homomorphism e to the continuous integral coefficient ring of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and any R-linear endomorphism f of the regular R-module, the endomorphism 1−ℓf is invertible. There are no noetherianity or finite dimensionality assumptions.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, Section 6.8, continuous coefficient realization and integral units

proof.text: Construct the continuous-ring comparison by adjunction from composition with the existing profiniteTestProjection, reusing its naturality and the pushforward-ring and affine weakly contractible detection helpers of CondensedFieldContinuousRealization. For an affine Spec R, explicitly identify maps to Spec LC(S,Z) with continuous maps to S: the forward map is the first spectrum coordinate, and the inverse is Spec of LocallyConstant.liftPrimeSpectrum (Int.castRingHom R). For the inverse law, localize at every prime. The characteristic idempotent of the fibre of a locally constant function maps to one, so the function equals its constant value locally; equality in all prime localizations proves equality in R. Transport along the affine isoSpec and the already proved relativeMapEquiv, then use the connected-components universal property. Projection naturality gives target naturality of this normalized correspondence. Bundle the actual component quotient using pointLanComponents and use the proved generic kanTerminal lemma: the inverse image of its identity is terminal in the Kan indexing category. Its composite with the test projection is the component quotient. Thus the Kan comparison is bijective, since continuous functions into a totally disconnected coefficient ring factor uniquely and continuously through connected components. The existing weakly contractible sheafification theorem makes the sheafification unit invertible. Left-adjoint uniqueness identifies the original comparison with this sheafified Kan comparison. Affine weakly contractible covers detect the resulting isomorphism globally.

A morphism of regular modules is sectionwise linear: applying the sheaf tensor comparison to the module action equation proves f_U(ab)=a f_U(b). Hence on every test object it is multiplication by the continuous integral function f_U(1).

The normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra is ultrametric, and ||ℓ||<1. Thus for every integral a, ||1−ℓa||=1. For a continuous integral-valued function a, its pointwise reciprocal (1−ℓa)⁻¹ is continuous, integral, and inverse on both sides. This constructs a unit without requiring completeness of E.

The integral coefficient ring is totally disconnected by the ultrametric topology. Use the continuous-ring comparison and sectionwise linearity to show every component of 1−ℓf is multiplication by a unit, hence bijective. Reflect the component isomorphisms through sheaves and internal module forgetting. Finally transport the result across e using the proved Mod.regularIsoOfIsIso comparison for restriction of scalars.

proof_origin.note: K1 repair, 2026-10-17: closes comparison_basis_isIso without new sorries. Reconstructs the normalized affine map correspondence from the current, proved liftPrimeSpectrum API instead of the removed profiniteLocallyConstantHomEquiv and canonicalComponentArrow helpers. Reuses generic kanTerminal, relativeMapEquiv, componentMapEquiv and the comparison/detection support already in the library. The comparison is an actual construction with proved inverse laws; no data is chosen from an undetermined existence theorem. Uses the existing point-components theorem only for the profinite structure on the actual quotient, and the existing weakly contractible sheafification theorem as a dependency. Local field freeness is not used.
